::: {#def-bonferroni}
#### Bonferroni correction

Given $m$ null hypotheses $H_1, \ldots, H_m$ with p-values $p_1, \ldots, p_m$ and a level $\siglevel$,
the **Bonferroni correction** rejects $H_j$ when its p-value is at most $\siglevel / m$:

$$\text{reject } H_j \iff p_j \le \frac{\siglevel}{m}.$$

Source: @james2021islr2e [ch. 13].
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#exm-bonferroni}
#### Bonferroni correction for the Khan genes

R functions for this page's procedures take the vector of p-values and a level, and return a logical vector.
For the Bonferroni correction with $\siglevel = 0.05$:

```{r}
#| label: bonferroni-reject
#| code-fold: false
bonferroni_reject <- function(p, alpha) p <= alpha / length(p)

alpha <- 0.05
c(
  threshold = alpha / m,
  rejections = sum(bonferroni_reject(khan_p, alpha))
)
```

With $m =$ `r m` tests the threshold is `r format(alpha / m, digits = 3)`,
and the correction rejects `r sum(bonferroni_reject(khan_p, alpha))` genes
out of the `r sum(khan_p <= 0.05)` with an unadjusted p-value of at most 0.05.
The same functions applied to the first ten genes of the data set show the arithmetic:
with $m = 10$ the threshold is $0.05 / 10 = 0.005$.

```{r}
#| label: bonferroni-ten-genes
fmt_p <- function(p) vapply(p, format, character(1), digits = 3)
ten_genes <- khan_p[1:10]
data.frame(
  gene = names(ten_genes),
  p_value = ten_genes,
  threshold = alpha / length(ten_genes),
  reject = bonferroni_reject(ten_genes, alpha),
  row.names = NULL
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(p_value) |>
  dplyr::mutate(p_value = fmt_p(p_value)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```
:::
